product.description: După ce a petrecut un timp îndelungat pe Riviera, împreună cu o comunitate americană expatriată, Kate Clephane decide să se întoarcă la New York, unde prezența îi fusese multă vreme refuzată de înalta societate, pentru vina de a-și fi abandonat soțul și fetița de trei ani. Cea care îi dorește întoarcerea este fiica sa, Anne, care vrea ca mama ei să îi fie alături la nunta cu Chris Fenno, erou de război, dar, în același timp, om fără talente deosebite și arivist de profesie. Kate este însă prea puțin interesată de adevăratele intenții ale lui Chris față de fiica ei, deoarece, în trecut, bărbatul i-a fost amant, iar ea este încă îndrăgostită de el. Dilema morală a femeii (să-i mărturisească fiicei sale secretul sau să tacă?) și drama ce va urma conduc spre un final care a scandalizat societatea americană la vremea apariției cărții.Există doar trei sau patru romancieri americani care pot fi considerați importanți –, iar Edith Wharton este unul dintre ei. Gore Vidal Adevărul e că nici un romancier al vremii noastre [...] nu a fost atât de neîndurător, atât de sarcastic, atât de aspru, cum a fost Edith Wharton când a atacat vulgaritatea și eșecurile societății noastre. Irving Howe

# Rivalitate: A Literary Drama of Society and Desire - Vol. 45

Immerse yourself in the complex world of high society with **Rivalitate. Vol. 45**, a captivating literary drama from Litera. This novel explores the intense conflicts that arise when personal desires collide with rigid social expectations, making it an essential read for fans of classic American fiction and deep character studies.

***

## The Conflict: Duty vs. Desire in New York Society

The story centers on Kate Clephane, a woman who has spent time enjoying life on the Riviera with an expatriate American community. However, she is forced to return to New Yorkâa city where her presence was long denied by high society due to the circumstances of her departure: abandoning both her husband and her three-year-old daughter.

Upon her return, Kate faces a difficult emotional landscape. Her own daughter, Anne, desperately hopes for her mother's presence at a wedding with Chris Fennoâa decorated war hero who, despite his achievements, lacks obvious unique talents and is merely successful by profession.

But what makes the situation deeply complicated is Kateâs hidden emotional history. She harbors unresolved feelings for Chris; he was once an intimate figure in her past, casting a long shadow over her current life choices. This creates a profound moral dilemma: should she reveal a secret to her daughter, or keep silent? The ensuing drama will ultimately lead to an outcome that scandalized American society at the time of the novel's original release.

## A Tapestry of Social Critique

This novel delves into universal themesâbetrayal, devotion, and the constraints placed upon women by societal norms. Like the great literary figures who captured the spirit of the era, *Rivalitate* offers a sharp and compelling look at the American elite.

The depth of social commentary is reminiscent of masters like Edith Wharton, whose work remains celebrated for its unflinching portrayal of class and decorum. As noted in appreciation of such literature, "There are only three or four American novelists who can be considered important... Edith Wharton was one of them. The truth is that no novelist of our time... has been as unsparing, as sarcastic, as sharp as Edith Wharton when attacking the vulgarity and failures of our society."

*Rivalitate. Vol. 45* invites readers to ponder where true love ends and social obligation begins. It promises a thrilling journey into moral ambiguity and passion.

***

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Is this a standalone novel or part of a series?**
While it is Volume 45, the narrative focuses on a complete dramatic arc, exploring deep character conflicts within the American high society setting.

**What makes this book so popular in literary circles?**
The novel's enduring appeal lies in its masterful blend of intense personal drama, unresolved romantic tension, and sharp social commentary that mirrors classic works by great authors like Edith Wharton.
